name: Compression framework (LZRAVEN)
verdict_reason: Apple states LZRAVEN decodes 3x faster than LZMA on Apple silicon at a slightly better ratio. It is new in OS 27, no independent numbers exist, and nothing contradicts the claim.
tier_reason: First-party documentation claim with no data set, device or method given.
claimed_speedup: Decodes 3x faster than COMPRESSION_LZMA on Apple silicon; encodes faster than LZMA (no number given)
platforms: iOS 27+, iPadOS 27+, macOS 27+, tvOS 27+, watchOS 27+, visionOS 27+
install: built into OS 27 releases (Compression framework, buffer API only)
one_liner: Apple's OS 27 high-ratio codec, documented as decoding 3x faster than LZMA at a similar or slightly better ratio.
how_it_is_fast: Apple describes LZ77 with an 8 MB dictionary, context-modeled entropy coding and near-optimal parsing, with a decoder that uses vector units to process several symbols per operation. LZMA's range decoder handles one bit at a time with serial dependencies, which limits its decode speed.
use_it_when: Apple-only payloads compressed once and decoded often, where LZMA's ratio is wanted but its decode time is too slow
skip_it_when: Data that must be readable by xz tools or non-Apple platforms
caveats: No published benchmark data, corpus or device
LZMA is not the default most apps use; compare against zlib or LZFSE if that is your current choice
tradeoffs: Requires OS 27 on every decoding device

evidence.quote: while decoding 3x faster on Apple silicon, where the decoder leverages vector units to process multiple symbols per operation.
